title: RKKY interaction as a probe of spin splitting and odd-parity nature in Floquet collinear magnets
authors: Hou-Jian Duan, Yong-Jia Wu, Xiaoliang Xiao, Ming-Xun Deng, Mou Yang, Rui-Qiang Wang
abstract: Odd-parity magnets were recently proposed to emerge in collinear antiferromagnets (AFMs) via Floquet engineering, with valley-dependent spin splitting underlying the odd-parity spin polarization. This proposal brings about two key challenges: detecting the spin splitting to verify the generation mechanism of these magnets, and identifying such polarization to confirm the odd-parity nature. Here, we show that the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction provides a unified magnetic probe for both tasks. Taking collinear $f$-wave magnets as a representative example, we find that the RKKY interaction yields distinct magnetic signals of the spin splitting---including a magnetism reversal in the Heisenberg/Ising terms and a sign alternation of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) term---that enable clear discrimination of collinear $f$-wave magnets from other related AFMs. Moreover, the DM term exhibits an $f$-wave shape with odd-parity symmetry, satisfying $J^{αβ}_{DM}(\mathbf{R}) = -J^{αβ}_{DM}(C_{2q}\mathbf{R})$ ($q=3$), which directly reflects the odd-parity spin polarization $S_z(\mathbf{k}) = -S_z(C_{2q}\mathbf{k})$ in momentum space. This behavior persists in $p$-wave magnets ($q=1$), demonstrating the generality of our approach. Our work establishes the RKKY interaction as a versatile probe for detecting band features of collinear odd-parity magnets, with predictions accessible to existing experimental techniques such as spin-polarized scanning tunneling spectroscopy.
summary: The paper demonstrates that the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction can act as a universal probe for characterizing exotic, odd-parity magnets generated in antiferromagnets using Floquet engineering. By analyzing distinct magnetic signatures within the RKKY coupling—such as specific sign changes and symmetry constraints on the DM term—the authors provide a clear theoretical pathway to experimentally verify these complex quantum states.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a method to detect both spin splitting and confirm the odd-parity nature of exotic magnets predicted to emerge in collinear antiferromagnets via Floquet engineering.
main_result: The RKKY interaction serves as a unified magnetic probe, yielding distinct signatures like magnetism reversals in Heisenberg/Ising terms and specific symmetries in the DM term that allow clear discrimination of these novel odd-parity magnets.
method: The study utilizes theoretical calculations based on the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, which is derived using Green's functions applied to effective Floquet Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The model focuses on collinear $f$-wave magnets realized in 2D collinear antiferromagnets on a honeycomb lattice, compared against baseline systems like graphene and standard AFMs. The physics is governed by an effective low-energy Floquet Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Distinct magnetic signals from the RKKY interaction: magnetism reversal in Heisenberg/Ising terms, sign alternation of the DM term, and confirmation of odd-parity symmetry ($\mathcal{J}^{	ext{DM}}(\mathbf{R}) = -\mathcal{J}^{	ext{DM}}(C_2^q\mathbf{R})$).
important_parameters: The analysis is performed in the high-frequency off-resonant regime of Floquet theory, and the results are shown to be general for $p$-wave magnets ($q=1$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that the RKKY interaction can effectively probe the underlying spin polarization features generated by the Floquet driving.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates band dispersions and Fermi surfaces for various magnetic systems (graphene, AFM, f-wave magnet). Figure 2 compares the calculated RKKY components ($J^H, J^I, J^{DM}$) versus impurity distance $R$ for different material types.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using Floquet engineering to generate odd-parity magnets. It then introduces and applies the RKKY interaction as a diagnostic tool, systematically comparing its calculated components across various magnetic models to isolate the unique signatures of the target f-wave magnet.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, symmetry-based theoretical diagnostic (RKKY) that links abstract concepts like odd-parity spin polarization and Floquet engineering to measurable magnetic responses accessible via techniques like STM spectroscopy.
